correctness.rationale: Contracting the specified triangle gives Petersen: for vertices 0 through 8 and the contracted vertex, the two-subset labels 34,15,24,35,45,25,23,13,14,12 give adjacency by disjointness. At scale one the filled triangle is a contractible subcomplex and its quotient is a connected graph with 10 vertices and 15 edges. The independent radius-two replay recomputed the face counts (12,51,96,87,51,19,3) from the vertex metric and checked the full proper-coface condition for each of 119 sequential elementary collapses. The residual complex has 12 vertices, 38 edges and 31 triangles. Contraction of the checked spanning tree gives one based vertex and 27 edge generators; at each of 27 checked steps a single-generator two-cell and its edge make a contractible subcomplex, so the quotient is a homotopy equivalence and deletes that generator from the other attaching words. The four remaining two-cells have trivial attaching maps. This proves a wedge of four 2-spheres, not merely four independent mod-two classes. The graph has diameter three; the zero stage is discrete and the third stage is a simplex. All distances are integral, and no degree has nonzero reduced homology at successive stages, so the listed half-open integral intervals are complete.
residual_risks: The classification concerns the vertex metric, not the continuum metric or a filtered homotopy equivalence. The supplied verifier was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: Tietze is a standard cubic graph, with a natural contrast to Petersen: a triangle expansion changes the scale-two Rips type from a simplex to a four-sphere wedge. Since homology ranks would not give this homotopy classification, the explicit integral certificate is useful as an exact test case for graph powers and as the intact baseline for fault comparisons. The routine endpoint stages complete the classification rather than constituting its value on their own.
residual_risks: This one triangle expansion is not evidence of a general expansion theorem.
